title: Social interaction test: a sensitive method for examining autism-related behavioral deficits
protocol: Change the bedding material in the home cage 24 hours or earlier before testing.
Weigh the novel mice and mark them on the tail 24 hours or earlier before testing.
Weigh the test mice and mark them on the tail at the time of the first injection of rapamycin.
Pair a test mouse with a novel mouse of the same sex, ensuring the novel mouse is not heavier than the test mouse by more than 5%.
Transfer the mice to the testing room.
Turn on ventilating fans in the sound-attenuating chamber.
Allow the mice to acclimate to the testing room for one hour or longer.
Clean the sound-attenuating chamber with 70% alcohol.
Move all cagemates of the test mouse to a novel cage.
Place the home cage of the test mouse alone with the camera, and leave the mouse undisturbed for fifteen minutes or longer.
Place the paired novel mouse into the home cage, and record behavior for ten minutes.
Remain outside the testing room during video recording to avoid disturbing the mouse's behavior.
Return the mice to their cagemates and remove the cage.
Repeat steps 8 to 14 if additional test mice are to be examined.
Watch the videos and score active interaction, defined as sniffing, close following, and allo-grooming.
Exclude aggressive behaviors from dependent measures.
